divergence_finding.headline: THE REAL WASTE IS A DIVERGENCE REGIME, NOT SEED NOISE. This supersedes and corrects the previous cycle's noise_floor_finding, which misdiagnosed the problem. 52% of full-rung compute produced garbage, and it is almost perfectly predicted by lr.
divergence_finding.method: All 379 full-rung (epochs=27) arms split on BPC < 3.0 (converged, n=181, median 2.3057) vs >= 3.0 (diverged, n=198, median 5.0745). Then divergence rate cross-tabulated by lr band.
divergence_finding.consequence_1_the_old_noise_floor_was_an: The previous cycle reported sigma=0.0299 BPC by pooling arms across ALL lr including the divergent ones. That number is not run-to-run noise - it is the tail of a bimodal distribution. Restricting to the converged regime (lr>=0.0012) and excluding diverged arms, the median within-config robust sigma is 0.0128 BPC, not 0.0299. So the sweep was ~2.3x LESS noisy than believed.
divergence_finding.consequence_2_but_noise_is_still_not_the: At the corrected sigma=0.0128, the top-12 full-rung spread is 0.0120 BPC = 0.94 sigma, and 18/108 converged-regime arms sit within 1 sigma of the record. Ranks 1-12 remain a coin flip. Replication is still required - but it is required to rank, not to avoid garbage.
divergence_finding.consequence_3_the_fix_is_narrow_lr_not_n: Because divergence is monotone in lr and reaches 0.0 at lr>=0.0014, the single highest-value search-space change is to move the lr range UP and make it discrete, so bayes/grid stops spending 52% of the budget on arms that cannot converge. This is worth more than any architecture-axis change.
divergence_finding.consequence_4_hyperband_eta3_cannot_save: Client-side Hyperband prunes on val/ce_final, so a diverged arm IS pruned early - which is why the wasted GPU-time is only 13% (78 of 608 GPU-hours) even though 52% of arms are garbage. The waste is in run COUNT and in the run_cap budget, not in wall-clock. Lowering run_cap from 160 to 96 while raising lr is therefore close to compute-neutral.

clw_finding.headline: REVERSAL OF THE PRIOR CYCLE'S clw STEERING DIRECTION. The previous cycle opened chunk_local_window to [null,32,64,128] and framed 'a moderate local window' as the win. The controlled GPU data says the axis is monotone toward MORE context, not less, so the new config centres it at [null,64,128,256].
clw_finding.gpu_controlled_pairs_none_vs_16: Converged budget-compliant arms, paired within identical (token_dec_dim_ff, chunk_dec_layers) cells - the only place a comparison is not confounded:
clw_finding.verdict: None beats clw=16 in ALL FOUR cells, by 0.165 to 0.405 BPC. This is the opposite sign from the previous cycle's framing, which cited the record run's clw=16 as weak evidence for small windows. The record run is a single unreplicated draw inside a cell whose own median is 2.6743 (n=7); its clw=16 is not what makes it fast.
clw_finding.tpu_side_agrees_and_is_monotone: None 2.2969 (n=4) > 64 2.0511 (n=7) > 128 1.9770 (n=2) > 256 1.9604 (n=27); the project's single best TPU run pvz94wfa (1.84410 BPC) uses clw=256.
clw_finding.both_sides_point_the_same_way: GPU says more-than-16 is better than 16. TPU says 256 > 128 > 64 > None. The only shape consistent with both is monotone increasing in window size, so the axis is centred high, not low.
clw_finding.operational_note: clw also nearly halves wall-clock (converged median runtime 5359s at clw=16 vs 12195s at clw=None), so it is a compute knob as well as an accuracy knob. Larger windows cost more time - which is the honest reason to treat this axis as a time-to-convergence trade, not free BPC.

depth_ladder_finding.cost_of_the_cap: cdl=8 (the cap) -> cdl=14 is -0.0289 BPC for 1.70x params and 1.36x runtime. At sigma=0.0128 that is 2.26 sigma - real, not noise. The ladder is monotone from 6 to 14 with only a +0.0026 blip at 12, well inside noise.
depth_ladder_finding.corrects_previous_cycles: The previous three cycles reported 'inflation is indistinguishable from free' and 'caps cost nothing'. That verdict was an artifact of min-of-N ranking over a noisy objective. Ranking by MEDIANS on a controlled, converged-only ladder shows depth genuinely helps. The correct statement is the opposite: the anti-GPT-ification cap on chunk_dec_layers costs roughly 0.03 BPC.
depth_ladder_finding.why_it_is_still_not_foldable: Because buying that 0.03 BPC requires 1.70x the parameters and 1.36x the wall-clock - that is precisely the compute inflation the guards forbid. The finding justifies KEEPING the cap (it is cheap insurance for 0.03 BPC) and it justifies spending the freed search budget on clw, which buys far more BPC at fixed compute.

lr_finding.headline: THE PRIOR CYCLE'S lr FIX WAS A TRADE THAT WAS NEVER PRICED. It raised lr to eliminate divergence, but divergence was already zero BELOW the new floor, and the raise itself costs BPC. This is the central correction of this cycle.

divergence_floor_is_0_00135_not_0_0014.method: All 362 full-rung (epochs=27) budget-compliant arms, divergence = val/best_bpc >= 3.0, binned at width 1e-5.
divergence_floor_is_0_00135_not_0_0014.result: Divergence reaches 0.00 at lr>=0.00135 and stays 0.00 through 0.00149. The prior cycle set the floor at 0.0014, one bin too high, and the sweep_config pinned {0.0014,0.0015}.

but_above_0_00140_bpc_gets_worse.penalty: +0.0629 BPC of converged median for lr>=0.00140, at zero divergence benefit (both bands are already 0.00 divergent). The higher-lr band is also MORE expensive per arm (0.94 vs 0.84 epoch-equivalents) because nothing gets pruned.

the_penalty_is_robust_not_an_outlier_art.method: Converged-median penalty of lr>=0.00140 over lr[0.00135,0.00140) under 12 successive controlled cuts, to rule out a single run driving it.
the_penalty_is_robust_not_an_outlier_art.verdict: Penalty is POSITIVE in 10 of 10 cuts that have data on both sides. It shrinks but never flips sign. Dropping the record run 65dr5rv3 does not change it (+0.0773 either way), so it is a distributional shift, not a winner's curse.
the_penalty_is_robust_not_an_outlier_art.why_it_happens: At fixed epochs the higher-lr arms reach a lower training loss but a WORSE validation BPC by the end of the cosine schedule - the schedule is being spent too hot, so annealing finishes before the val curve turns. This is the same 'LR integral vs fixed epochs' mechanism the TPU agent diagnosed independently on PR #206 (val plateaus E33-E40 while train/loss keeps falling). Two agents, two hardware, same mechanism.

lr_finding.what_was_actually_wasting_budget: NOT lr. Epoch-equivalents per arm by lr band (full-rung pool, total 161 epoch-equivalents over 362 arms): lt0.0009 0.24, 0.0009-0.0011 0.28, 0.0011-0.0012 0.45, 0.0012-0.0013 0.75, 0.0013-0.0014 0.80, >=0.0014 0.94. Client-side Hyperband already prunes the low-lr arms at 24-28% of the rungs they would have consumed. The run-count waste is real; the GPU-time waste is not. That was the prior cycle's own conclusion_4 and it still holds - the new finding is that the FIX it chose for that waste was mispriced.
